name: CarryCtx
summary: A local-first project lifecycle control layer that persists agent and human collaboration state in SQLite, integrates Git-aware workspaces and checkpoints, and exchanges validated state through mergeable local snapshots.
scope: agent, team, session, and handoff coordination
ctxpack export, import, and local snapshot merge

features.name: Local SQLite project state
features.description: CarryCtx stores authoritative project state in a SQLite database at <git-common-dir>/carryctx/state.sqlite, shared by linked worktrees, while .carryctx/ holds project configuration and guidance.
benefits: One durable state boundary for a repository and its linked worktrees
Queryability without a hosted service
Schema migrations and integrity checks are part of the CLI contract
costs: State depends on local filesystem and SQLite availability
Shared linked-worktree state requires database coordination
Migration compatibility is an operational responsibility

features.name: Guarded task lifecycle and dependency gating
features.description: Tasks use explicit planned, ready, in-progress, blocked, review, completed, and cancelled states; transition evaluation gates claim, start, unblock, and completion on ownership, dependency, session, progress, and policy facts.
benefits: Explicit readiness and terminal-state behavior
Strong prerequisites cannot be bypassed at key transitions
Typed refusal paths for invalid lifecycle changes
costs: Many state and guard combinations must be understood
The lifecycle constrains workflows outside its transition policy
Dependency and completion policy can reject an executable command

lifecycle.notes: The fixed CarryCtx task source and lifecycle documentation directly record explicit task states and guarded transitions for the cited revision.

features.name: Durable collaboration records
features.description: Agents, teams, sessions, progress items, checkpoints, handoffs, decisions, and append-only events are persisted as project records so responsibility and recovery context survive changes of harness, window, session, and worktree.
benefits: Separates durable identity from an agent runtime
Handoffs, review context, and audit history are queryable
Resume and context projections support recovery
costs: Record schemas and references add coordination overhead
Persistent history requires cleanup and migration policies
The external harness still owns scheduling and model selection

features.name: Capability-aware VCS workspaces and checkpoints
features.description: CarryCtx uses a VcsBackend boundary for repository discovery, status, workspace creation and removal, and snapshots Git-aware checkpoint state; Git is the Tier 1 backend and Jujutsu is an optional runtime backend with fail-closed behavior for unsupported operations.
benefits: Version-control operations have an explicit capability boundary
Checkpoints preserve branch, head, dirty, changed-file, and diff information
Unsupported Jujutsu operations do not silently become Git operations
costs: Checkpoint meaning depends on repository and backend behavior
Multiple VCS backends require capability-specific policies
Cleanup must account for sessions, dirty state, and colocated layouts

features.name: Context graph and dependency extraction
features.description: CarryCtx models generic graph nodes and edges alongside core entities, and exposes graph scanning, dependency extraction, linking, and edge queries for code and project context.
benefits: Tasks, files, modules, decisions, and bugs can be related explicitly
Impact and context-gathering queries are supported
Graph metadata is extensible through JSON fields
costs: Generic edges require relation-type discipline
A graph projection can become stale
Name resolution needs ambiguity handling

features.name: Validated ctxpack state exchange and local merge
features.description: CarryCtx exports validated directory-form ctxpack bundles, records export-parent DAGs and tombstones, and can stage a fail-closed three-way merge with conflict resolution and local Git snapshot references without making Git transport part of the binary.
benefits: Parallel local state exchange is explicit and reviewable
Identity, deletion evidence, and merge-base provenance are preserved
Unresolved conflicts are staged while live state is protected
costs: Merge correctness depends on identity and compatibility rules
Clock-based election and degraded two-way merges have limits
External transport is required between machines

features.name: Zero-network core boundary
features.description: The core binary is local-first and does not initiate network connections; persistence, Git, files, and local subprocesses stay inside the boundary while Git push/fetch and other byte transport remain external responsibilities.
benefits: Project state stays offline
Transport and state semantics compose separately
The core trust and dependency surface stays small
costs: Multi-machine workflows require external transport
Local whole-file sync is last-writer-wins
Offline operation provides no centralized coordination

mathematical_views.question: Which task, ownership, dependency, session, and progress facts permit each lifecycle transition, and which transitions are terminal or refused?
assumptions: Project state is represented by task, dependency, agent, session, and progress records
Guards observe a consistent SQLite state before applying a command
External scheduling and human judgment are outside the system
Typed errors are refused transitions rather than state changes

lifecycle.notes: Candidate lifecycle model proposed from the cited task transition and guard documentation; external scheduling and human judgment remain explicit assumptions.

mathematical_views.question: How do durable entity rows, checkpoints, progress records, and append-only events provide a recoverable projection of project activity?
assumptions: State-changing commands append documented events in the same transaction as state updates
Events are historical records and are not rewritten by ordinary projections
SQLite locking and migration internals are abstracted
A checkpoint is bounded recovery context, not a complete database backup

mathematical_views.model: Export-parent DAG and three-way row merge
mathematical_views.question: How can independent local state snapshots select a deterministic common ancestor and produce a conflict-aware merged state?
assumptions: Export identifiers are lexicographically stable and parent links form an acyclic history
Rows have stable identity keys and required deletes have tombstones
The engine compares base, ours, and theirs before per-table policies
A degraded two-way merge is distinct from a resolved three-way merge

mathematical_views.model: Typed context graph with projected code dependencies
mathematical_views.question: How do task, file, module, decision, and bug nodes plus typed edges support context and impact queries over a changing project?
assumptions: Node identifiers are stable within project state and edge types have defined meanings
Dependency extraction is a projection that may require rescanning
Queries report recorded relationships and do not prove code correctness
SQLite query planning and parser details are abstracted

benefits: Low-deployment local durability and queryability
costs: Shared local state and migrations require database coordination

benefits: Explicit readiness, ownership, and terminal-state invariants
costs: Policy guards add workflow states and refusal cases

benefits: Handoffs and recovery context survive runtime changes
costs: Persistent history increases schema responsibility

benefits: Git evidence and isolation are visible at lifecycle boundaries
costs: Backend capabilities constrain cleanup

benefits: Explicit relationships improve context discovery
costs: Graph maintenance and relation semantics can become stale

benefits: Parallel state can be exchanged with conflict evidence
costs: Merge policies and compatibility rules add complexity

benefits: Small offline trust boundary
costs: Users must operate external transport

relations.notes: CarryCtx invokes local Git operations for repository discovery, workspaces, checkpoints, and optional local snapshot refs; Git remains a separate implementation boundary.
CarryCtx uses an embedded SQLite database for authoritative project state; this records an implementation dependency, not equivalence with SQLite.

Both systems make durable, inspectable execution state and lifecycle transitions explicit: CarryCtx records project tasks, dependencies, sessions, progress, and checkpoints, while Temporal records workflow execution history and replay-relevant transitions. This is a bounded structural analogy, not implementation reuse, equivalence, or historical influence.
